subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Moore's Law: Doubling Every Two Years
description: A short lesson to help you apply Moore's Law: Doubling Every Two Years.

hook.text: In 1965 Gordon Moore predicted transistor counts would double roughly every two years.

buildup.text: Smaller transistors mean more per chip, faster switching, and lower cost per function.

discovery.text: The prediction held for decades: 2,300 transistors in 1971, 50 billion by 2020.

twist.text: Moore's law is an economic observation, not a physics law. It could stop any time.

climax.text: Shrinking below 3 nm pushes against atomic limits. Quantum effects start to interfere.

punchline.text: Fifty years of doubling — the most consequential prediction in tech history.

quiz.question: What does Moore's law predict?
options: The number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years
The cost of silicon wafers halves every decade
